item.title: Probing high-momentum components in $^{16}$O via zero-degree $(p,d)$ cross-section ratios
item.description: arXiv:2610.13243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The $^{16}$O$(p,d)^{15}$O reaction was measured at zero degrees for incident-proton energies of 403, 604, 907 and 1209 MeV. Cross-section ratios for the 6.18-MeV (3/2$^-$) and 5.24-MeV (5/2$^+$) excited-state transitions, normalized to the ground-state transition, were previously reported in Wang et al., Phys. Lett. B 879, 140563 (2026), doi:10.1016/j.physletb.2026.140563, together with their implications for high-momentum neutron components in $^{16}$O. The present work extends that study by providing additional experimental and data-analysis details, and by reporting for the first time the ratio $R_{7.3}$, defined as the cross section populating the 7.28-MeV (7/2$^+$) state relative to that for the ground state. The positive-parity state ratios exhibit a pronounced momentum dependence, consistent with representative variational Monte Carlo trends.

item.title: Application and Optimization of the GET Electronics System for Double-Sided Silicon Strip Detector Readout
item.description: arXiv:2610.12923v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Double-sided silicon strip detectors (DSSDs) are widely used for charged-particle detection in nuclear reaction experiments. However, the large number of readout channels associated with DSSDs places stringent demands on front-end electronics and data acquisition systems, particularly in experiments employing large detector arrays. In this work, we investigate the application and optimization of the Generic Electronics for Time Projection Chambers (GET) system for multi-channel DSSD readout. Through optimization of the DC-blocking capacitors on the custom-designed interface board and waveform-based energy extraction algorithms, the readout system achieves an energy resolution of {\sigma} = 22 keV for 5.49 MeV alpha particles. Its performance is further validated in a representative nuclear physics experiment employing charged-particle telescopes. The results demonstrate that the GET system provides a versatile and scalable waveform-sampling solution for multi-channel DSSD readout.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Nucl. Instrum. Methods Phys. Res. A1091(2026) 171772

item.title: Dijet hadrochemistry: tomography of jet-induced medium excitation and diffusion wake
item.description: arXiv:2610.13046v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Energetic partons traversing the quark-gluon plasma in relativistic heavy-ion collisions induce a medium response that modifies the production of associated hadrons, whose chemical composition provides a sensitive probe of this response. We study jet-associated hadrochemistry using the coupled linear Boltzmann transport and hydrodynamics model with a hybrid hadronization scheme that combines Cooper--Frye particlization, quark coalescence and string fragmentation. For inclusive charged jets in $p+p$ and 0--10\% central Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.02$~TeV, the calculated in-cone $K/\pi$ and $p/\pi$ ratios are enhanced in Pb+Pb relative to $p+p$ collisions, consistent with preliminary ALICE measurements, with coalescence between shower and thermal partons providing a substantial contribution. Extending the analysis to dijet events, we predict that both ratios are enhanced around the leading and subleading jets, more strongly around the subleading jet and more pronounced for larger radial size. After mixed-event acceptance correction and sideband background subtraction, the yields of associated pions, kaons and protons all become negative near $|\Delta\phi|\simeq\pi/2$, signaling a depletion caused by the diffusion wake. The $K/\pi$ and $p/\pi$ ratios of these deficits remain finite and exceed the $p+p$ values around the jet peaks, indicating that the missing hadrons originate from jet-excited medium. These results establish dijet hadrochemistry as an experimentally accessible tomographic probe of jet-induced medium excitation and the diffusion wake.
item.dc:creator: Cong Yi, Xiang-Yu Wu, Zhong Yang, Pi Duan, Guang-You Qin, Xin-Nian Wang, Wenbin Zhao

item.title: Octupole correlations in the excited $0^+$ states and two-neutron transfers in actinide nuclei
item.description: arXiv:2610.13048v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Impacts of octupole correlations on low-energy excited $0^+$ states and two-neutron transfer intensities in Ra and Th isotopes are analyzed within the interacting boson model, using the Hamiltonian parameters that are obtained from microscopic nuclear density functional theory calculations. Incorporating the octupole degree of freedom in the model is shown to give an overall reasonable description of the ground-state-band energy levels and to lower the $0^+_2$ ones significantly. The calculation yields a number of excited $0^+$ states, most of which are formed by the configurations of more than one octupole boson. Octupole correlations make significant contributions to the $0^+_1 \to 0^+_2$ $(p,t)$ and $(t,p)$ transfer intensities in those nuclei in which the octupole collectivity is most enhanced. Behaviors of the predicted transfer intensities with the increasing neutron number along the isotopic chain reflect nuclear structural evolution.
item.dc:creator: Kosuke Nomura

item.title: nCTEQ26 nuclear parton distribution functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.13633v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present the new release of nuclear parton distribution functions (nPDFs) from the nCTEQ collaboration: nCTEQ26. In this global analysis, we combine our recent, more selective studies of different experimental measurements and extend them to determine a modern set of nPDFs based on the largest selection of data considered to date. This selection includes neutral- and charged-current deep-inelastic scattering (DIS), fixed-target Drell-Yan, and a large variety of collider data from RHIC and LHC Runs I and II. On the theoretical side, we match this considerably extended kinematic range with a new nPDF parametrization that combines a flexible functional form of the x-dependence with a quadratic logarithmic nuclear A-dependence as well as target-mass and deuteron corrections for the reliable inclusion of high-x DIS data. Following our previous successful work, we partially employ a data-driven approach that allows us to not only include open heavy-quark data, but also quarkonium data. In addition, we establish the consistency of this approach by comparing it to an alternative fit based on perturbative predictions of open heavy-quark data alone. We determine the uncertainties of our nCTEQ26 nPDFs with a Hessian error analysis, test their reliability by comparing our nPDFs to other, similar recent analyses, and make predictions for current and future experimental measurements that have not been included in the analysis.
item.dc:creator: nCTEQ Collaboration, K. Greve, T. Je\v{z}o, A. Kusina, J. Wissmann, M. Klasen, K. Kova\v{r}\'ik, C. L\'eger, J. G. Morf\'in, F. I. Olness, P. Risse, I. Schienbein, J. Y. Yu

item.title: Final-state centrality in relativistic heavy-ion simulations from neural networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.13828v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Experiments in relativistic heavy-ion collisions determine centrality from final-state quantities, usually the charged-particle multiplicity. Performing the same in hydrodynamic simulations requires millions of events, which is impractical for state-of-the-art hybrid models, and centrality is therefore commonly approximated by the initial entropy or energy. We show that neural networks trained on a few hundred hybrid events predict the event-by-event multiplicity and mean transverse momentum $[p_T]$ with relative errors of 1--2\%, which makes it possible to generate millions of collisions at a small fraction of the cost of the full simulation. For Pb--Pb collisions at $2.76$~TeV and Au--Au collisions at $200$~GeV, the initial-state and final-state definitions select nearly the same events in 10\%-wide classes, but up to 20\% of the events change class when the classes are 1\% wide. We then compute the fluctuations of $[p_T]$ and its Pearson correlations with a proxy of the elliptic flow, estimated from the initial eccentricity, and with multiplicity. The first correlation is insensitive to how centrality is defined, while the second changes substantially. The approach can be applied at every design point of Bayesian analyses at modest additional cost.
item.dc:creator: Anibal Bezerra, Fernando G. Gardim

item.title: Impact of ab initio E1 strength on neutron capture rates along the nickel isotopic chain
item.description: arXiv:2610.13868v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Nucleosynthesis simulations of the r-process require neutron capture rates for neutron-rich nuclei, many of which lie beyond experimental reach. Predicting these rates relies on theoretical calculations of the low-energy electric dipole (E1) strength near the neutron threshold. We present the first ab initio computation of the E1 strength along the nickel isotopic chain, for $^{58}$Ni and the even-even isotopes $^{68-80}$Ni. The E1 strength is obtained with the Lorentz integral transform coupled-cluster (LIT-CC) method, extended to axially symmetric reference states to reach open-shell nuclei, using two- and three-nucleon interactions from chiral effective field theory. The approach is benchmarked against the measured photoabsorption cross section of $^{58}$Ni and the E1 strength of $^{68}$Ni. Along the chain we find low-lying E1 strength above the neutron threshold that grows with neutron number. Including it in the reaction code TALYS enhances the neutron capture rates forming $^{68-78}$Ni between 3 and 10 GK, with an effect that increases with temperature and neutron number and an uncertainty dominated by the inversion of the integral transform. For $^{80}$Ni, where strong pygmy dipole strength lies just above threshold, the enhancement sets in already around 0.5 GK. Together, these results open the way to ab initio input for neutron capture rates along isotopic chains far from stability.
item.dc:creator: Francesca Bonaiti, Joanna E. Sobczyk

item.title: News from NA61/SHINE
item.description: arXiv:2609.08483v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: NA61/SHINE is a multi-purpose, fixed-target hadron spectrometer at the CERN SPS. Its research program includes studies of strong interactions, as well as reference measurements for neutrino and cosmic-ray physics. A significant advantage of NA61/SHINE over collider experiments is its extended coverage of phase space available for particle production. This contribution summarizes recent selected results from our strong interaction program. These include rapidity spectra of $K^+$ and $\pi^-$ mesons in Xe+La reactions compared to other collision systems, energy dependence of the scaled $\pi^-$ total yield (the `kink` plot) in Xe+La compared to other collision systems and models, $\phi$(1020) rapidity spectra in Ar+Sc collisions compared to models, $\Lambda$ transverse polarization in p+p reactions, energy dependence of intensive quantities of net-electric charge distribution in Ar+Sc collisions compared to p+p results, as well as an update on the evidence of large violation of isospin symmetry in kaon production --- the excess of charged over neutral kaons.
item.dc:creator: SHINE Collaboration

item.title: Toward testing antinucleon$\unicode{x2013}$nucleus optical potentials with antineutron scattering lengths
item.description: arXiv:2608.18668v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The antineutron$\unicode{x2013}$nucleus scattering length is currently known only indirectly, via antiproton$\unicode{x2013}$nucleus optical potentials fitted to level shifts and widths of antiprotonic atoms. The antineutron$\unicode{x2013}$nucleus and antiproton$\unicode{x2013}$nucleus potentials are related to each other through charge symmetry. We calculate the scattering length from optical potentials proposed for antiprotonic atoms using nucleon density distributions as input. We find that the scattering length for an $N>Z$ nuclide is largely affected by the poorly constrained neutron density distribution and by a possible isovector interaction, one of the mechanisms introduced to reproduce the isotope dependence of antiprotonic $^{40,48}\mathrm{Ca}$ data. For $^{48}\mathrm{Ca}$, the isovector term modifies the scattering length by $0.3\unicode{x2013}0.4\,\mathrm{fm}$ ($0.4\unicode{x2013}0.5\,\mathrm{fm}$) for the real (imaginary) part, an order of magnitude beyond the uncertainty propagated from the isoscalar potential. As no antineutron$\unicode{x2013}$nucleus scattering data are available below $76\,\mathrm{MeV}/c$, a direct measurement with recently proposed low-energy antineutron beams would provide the first access to the antinucleon$\unicode{x2013}$nucleus interaction in the $s$-wave regime.
item.dc:creator: Hiroyuki Fujioka, Sayaka Ishii

item.title: Full-event anomaly detection for new physics searches at the Electron-Ion Collider
item.description: arXiv:2610.00308v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The future Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) will offer new opportunities to search for physics beyond the Standard Model. We study resonant anomaly detection using machine learning and the full particle content of an event. We consider a new neutral gauge boson and a heavy neutral lepton as illustrative signals with different electron-jet topologies. Weakly supervised learning uses this event information to enhance the sensitivity of an invariant-mass search without identifying individual signal events during training. Comparisons with high-level observables show that the electron kinematics account for an important part of the separation, while correlations among the particles provide further sensitivity. We also construct a conditional full-event generator by adapting a model pretrained on LHC jets to produce EIC background events. A scan over signal fractions demonstrates substantial signal enhancement using the learned background reference, providing a proof of concept for this approach at the EIC. Finally, we consider a fully unsupervised graph autoencoder that provides modest signal enhancement but retains sensitivity at signal fractions too small for effective weak supervision. Our results motivate full-event anomaly detection as part of the EIC physics program and identify directions for developing methods suited to its distinct kinematics.
item.dc:creator: Dimitrios Athanasakos, Sebastian Grieninger, Hongkai Liu, Tymothy Mangan, Felix Ringer, Robert Szafron

item.title: Novel chiral-wobbling excitation mode in atomic nuclei
item.description: arXiv:2610.09808v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The properties of high-spin band structures in $^{74}$Br nucleus are investigated using the triaxial projected shell model (TPSM) and particle triaxial rotor (PTR) approaches. It has already been demonstrated that lowest three bands observed in $^{74}$Br have a characteristic feature of a chiral-wobbler. The first excited band is the chiral partner of the yrast band and the second excited band is the wobbling band based on the yrast state. We have analyzed the third excited band using the TPSM and PTR calculated quantities, and a unique character of this band is revealed. It is predicted that this band is the chiral partner of the second excited band, and is also a wobbling mode based on the first excited band.
item.dc:creator: Kouser Qureshie, S. P. Rouoof, J. A. Sheikh, Nazira Nazir, G. H. Bhat, S. Jehangir, N. A. Rather, R. J. Guo, S. Y. Wang, C. Liu, Q. B. Chen, S. Frauendorf
